subject: english-literature
topicDisplay: Paper 1 Exploring Modern And Literary Heritage Texts
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When tracking a theme across a whole text, the strongest approach is to...
options: Quote only from the final page
Trace how the theme develops and changes from beginning to end
Mention the theme once in your introduction
questions.explain: Examining how a theme is introduced, developed and resolved shows a 'whole-text' understanding that examiners reward.

questions.q: A 'caesura' is a deliberate pause within a line of poetry. Which is the BEST analytical comment on its effect?
options: It forces a break that can fragment the rhythm and emphasise the words around it
It always signals the end of the poem
It guarantees the poem is a sonnet
It tells us the poet's date of birth
questions.explain: A caesura interrupts the line's flow, drawing attention to surrounding words and sometimes mirroring disruption or hesitation.

questions.q: In what order do the three Christmas spirits visit Scrooge?
questions.explain: The Ghosts of Christmas Past, then Present, then Yet to Come visit him in that sequence.

questions.q: What is a 'volta' in a sonnet?
options: A turn or shift in argument, tone or feeling
The opening line that states the subject
The rhyming couplet at the very end only
questions.explain: The volta is the 'turn' where the poem changes direction in thought or mood, often signalled by words like 'but' or 'yet'.

questions.q: A 'stanza' is to a poem what a ____ is to prose.
questions.explain: A stanza groups lines into a unit, much as a paragraph groups sentences in prose.

questions.q: What is the central theme of Scrooge's journey through the novella?
questions.explain: Scrooge is redeemed, transforming from miser to a generous, caring man.

questions.q: Who is Tiny Tim and why is he significant?
options: Bob Cratchit's ill, kind-hearted youngest child
questions.explain: Tiny Tim is Bob Cratchit's sickly, gentle son whose possible death moves Scrooge toward change.

questions.q: What warning does Marley's ghost give Scrooge about his own future?
options: That his house is haunted forever
That he wears a heavier chain and will be visited by three spirits
That Bob Cratchit will leave him
That he will lose all his money
questions.explain: Marley warns that Scrooge forges an even heavier chain and that three spirits will visit to offer him a chance to escape his fate.

questions.q: 'Juxtaposition' is a technique in which a writer...
options: Repeats the same word three times
Places two contrasting ideas or images close together for effect
questions.explain: Juxtaposition sets contrasting elements side by side to highlight differences and provoke thought.

questions.q: What is Fred's relationship to Scrooge?
questions.explain: Fred is Scrooge's good-natured nephew who repeatedly invites him to Christmas dinner.

questions.q: How was Sheila Birling responsible for Eva Smith's misfortune?
options: She reported her to the police
She had Eva dismissed from a shop out of jealousy
questions.explain: Sheila got Eva sacked from Milwards in a fit of jealous temper.

questions.q: In an allegory, characters and events...
options: Stand symbolically for wider ideas or moral/political meanings
Are described in great factual detail
questions.explain: An allegory works on two levels: the literal story carries a deeper symbolic or moral meaning.

questions.q: When the gentlemen ask Scrooge to give to the poor early on, what does he suggest they rely on instead?
questions.explain: Scrooge points to "the prisons" and "the workhouses", echoing harsh Victorian Poor Law attitudes.

questions.q: How does Scrooge behave on Christmas morning after the spirits' visits?
options: He returns to work as usual
He is joyful and sends a large turkey to the Cratchits
questions.explain: A transformed Scrooge laughs with delight and anonymously sends a prize turkey to Bob Cratchit's family.

questions.q: A 'semantic field' refers to...
options: The opening line of a play
A group of words linked by a shared area of meaning
questions.explain: A semantic field is a cluster of words relating to one theme, such as words of war or of disease, that shapes tone.

questions.q: A 'foil' is a character who...
options: Contrasts with another to highlight that character's qualities
questions.explain: A foil's contrasting traits throw another character's qualities into sharper relief.

questions.q: Who is Bob Cratchit?
questions.explain: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's poorly paid, overworked but warm-hearted clerk.

questions.q: What scene from Scrooge's youth does the Ghost of Christmas Past show that explains his loneliness?
options: His sister Fan fetching him home from a lonely boarding school
questions.explain: The spirit shows young Scrooge alone at school until his loving sister Fan arrives to bring him home.

questions.q: A 'tricolon' is a rhetorical device in which a writer...
options: Uses three parallel words, phrases or clauses for emphasis
Pauses three times in one line
questions.explain: A tricolon groups three parallel elements to create rhythm, emphasis and a satisfying sense of completeness.

questions.q: What does the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come show Scrooge?
options: Visions of his lonely death and neglected grave
questions.explain: It shows Scrooge's own death, his unmourned grave, and people indifferent to his passing.

questions.q: What broader social concern does Dickens press through the figures of Ignorance and Want?
options: Society's neglect of poor children and the need for education and care
questions.explain: Dickens warns that neglecting poor children, especially through ignorance, breeds doom unless society takes responsibility.

questions.q: By the end of the novella, how is Scrooge changed in relation to Tiny Tim?
options: He sends him to a workhouse
He becomes "a second father" to Tiny Tim
questions.explain: Dickens writes that to Tiny Tim, who did not die, Scrooge "was a second father".
